algorithms.name: Matching a search
steps: Split what was typed into words on spaces; ignore case and surrounding punctuation; fewer than two characters in total lists nothing.
A setting matches when every typed word is the start of some word in its label, description, section name or scope name.
Order: settings where every typed word starts a word in the label, then the rest; within each, App, then Project, then agent settings, then section order, then row order.
An agent setting is one result regardless of how many agents there are; its agent list is the project's non-archived agents in roster order.

design:
D1 One shared `SettingsSection` / `SettingsRow` pair (`hub/ui/src/components/environment/SettingsSection.tsx`) serves project and per-agent settings; its `scope` eyebrow says which.

D2 The update body is derived from `ProjectSettings` with every field optional (`ProjectSettingsUpdate` in `hub/hub/api/v1/projects.py`), so a field cannot be accepted and then silently not written; the handler merges onto stored values with `exclude_unset` and validates the merged object.

D3 Steppers are removed in CSS (`hub/ui/src/index.css`), not by changing input types, so browser validation still applies.
lifecycle: Imported from openspec 2026-10-07; overhauled 2026-10-08 against the code at e25e059.
problem: Per-project configuration moved out of the navigation rail into Environment sections. Those sections must read as complete, show what each setting does, never silently revert settings the surface did not know about, and say whether a save worked.

requirements.rationale: A section with few settings should still read as complete, and the operator should know whether it is project or agent configuration.
requirements.statement: Every configuration section SHALL open with its scope, its title and a short statement of what it governs.

requirements.rationale: Rows scan quickly and keep the explanation next to the control it explains.
requirements.statement: A configuration section SHALL present its settings as rows, each pairing a label and an explanation of the setting's effect with its control, separated by hairlines rather than each enclosed in a card.

requirements.rationale: A narrow column in a wide pane reads as unfinished.
requirements.statement: A configuration section SHALL fill the content region it is given, bounding text and controls to a readable measure without leaving a large unused region beside a narrow column.

requirements.rationale: Steppers invite accidental changes on hover and scroll; removing them must not remove validation.
requirements.statement: Numeric settings SHALL be typed, with no increment or decrement steppers in any browser engine, and SHALL keep their numeric constraints, an invalid value being refused with an explanation.

requirements.rationale: The note on an unmerged task sends the operator to settings to choose a branch; the control it names has to be there.
requirements.statement: The Landing section SHALL offer a main-branch control showing the project's chosen branch, offering the repository's detected branch as a one-click suggestion when none is chosen, and disabled with an explanation when the project is not a git repository.

requirements.rationale: A surface that must resend every setting can silently revert one it does not know about, which is how a save once cleared a project's checkpoint configuration.
requirements.statement: `PUT /projects/{id}/settings` SHALL accept a body naming only the fields being changed, treating an omitted field as unchanged and an explicit null as a clear, and SHALL apply cross-field validation to the merged result.

requirements.rationale: Budget changes made in Accounting were already in the project's history; the same change made in Settings must be too (F238).
requirements.statement: A settings save that changes at least one value SHALL persist a `project_settings_updated` event listing each changed field's previous and new value, and a save that changes nothing SHALL record nothing.

requirements.rationale: These references are not foreign keys, so the route is the only place a cross-project or deleted runner can be caught.
requirements.statement: A settings save naming a conversation-title runner or checkpoint runner that does not exist in this project SHALL be refused with 400 naming the runner ID.

requirements.rationale: The Hub checks it only in request_agent (api/v1/agents.py:2556); the current label promises a limit that does not exist (F557).
requirements.statement: Wherever agent budget is labelled (Settings and Overview), the text MUST say it caps how many agents the project may hold when an agent staffs a new one, and MUST NOT say it limits agents running at the same time.

requirements.rationale: The page and agents read one list; a job that has never been configured is still a job the operator can turn on.
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/manager/jobs MUST answer 200 with {"jobs": [...]}, one entry per registered job in registry order, each with key, title, description, trigger, enabled, runner_id and model; a job with no stored row MUST be listed with enabled false and runner_id and model null.

requirements.rationale: Same validation as the project settings route applies to conversation_title_runner_id today (projects.py:516-528).
requirements.statement: PATCH /api/v1/projects/{id}/manager/jobs/{key} with any of enabled, runner_id and model MUST store them and answer the job as listed; an unknown key MUST answer 404, and a runner_id that is not one of this project's runners MUST answer 400 and change nothing.

requirements.rationale: Most title calls end before a spawn (already titled from this excerpt, F422); recording those would bury the firings that cost something.
requirements.statement: Every manager spawn MUST record one manager_job_fired event holding job, trigger, subject (for titles, the conversation id), runner_id, cli, model, outcome (written, empty or failed), detail (for titles, the title written), duration_ms and usage (null when the runner reports none). An exit before any spawn MUST record nothing.

requirements.rationale: A background agent whose work cannot be inspected is the hardest kind to trust (R5).
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/manager/activity MUST answer {"firings": [...]}, newest first, at most limit entries (default 50, at most 200), optionally filtered by job.

requirements.rationale: turn_scheduler.schedule_agent and trigger_agent_directly gate on a running Run under the agent's name (conversation_titles.py:7-13).
requirements.statement: A manager firing MUST NOT create a Run row or hold an agent name, so it never makes an agent look busy or delays that agent's queue.

requirements.rationale: The settings body forbids unknown fields (projects.py:84), so an app window still running the old bundle would otherwise fail to save any project setting until reloaded; existing clients and tests keep their contract.
requirements.statement: GET and PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/settings MUST keep conversation_title_mode and conversation_title_runner_id: reading reports generate when the conversation-titles job is enabled and its runner_id, and writing sets the job's enabled flag and runner_id.

requirements.rationale: It runs on :8000's real database at its next restart; titles must keep behaving as configured, and rolling back must lose nothing that existed before.
requirements.statement: The migration MUST create manager_jobs and give every project whose conversation_title_mode is generate or whose conversation_title_runner_id is set a conversation-titles row (enabled exactly when the mode is generate, runner_id copied, model null); its downgrade MUST write each row's enabled flag and runner_id back to the project columns and drop the table.

requirements.rationale: A committed bundle reaches :8000's app on its next reload, possibly before its server restarts.
requirements.statement: The app's Environment MUST have a Manager section listing each job with an on/off control, a runner select and a model select, and below them the activity list; the Settings section MUST no longer show the conversation title controls. Where the Hub answers 404 for the manager routes, the section MUST say this Hub has no manager yet instead of failing.

requirements.rationale: An operator who doubts a judgement needs what was answered, not only a count (F581).
requirements.statement: Each manager_job_fired event for a firing that spawned a model MUST keep the model's answer as answer: its raw text when the worker returned one, otherwise its parsed answer as JSON, cut to its first 8,000 characters and ending in a marker saying it was cut; a firing whose spawn returned nothing MUST keep answer null. GET /manager/activity MUST list it with the firing.

requirements.rationale: Sideways scroll hides controls entirely; the audit found three sections doing it at 1024px.
requirements.statement: At window widths of 960px and wider, in dark and light mode, no App, Project or Agent settings section scrolls horizontally or places any text or control outside the window, when its values are long values as defined in this document.

requirements.rationale: Agent Context and Workspace showed a description one word per line because the control beside it would not give up width.
requirements.statement: Where a setting's label and description sit beside its control, the text column is at least 240px wide; when the control cannot fit beside text of that width, the control moves below the text and takes the row's width instead.

requirements.rationale: End-truncation hid exactly the part of a worktree path that differs between rows.
requirements.statement: A long value shown read-only (a path, command, id, branch or model id) either wraps or is shortened in the middle keeping its beginning and its last segment, and its full value is shown on hover; a path or id can also be copied whole in one action.

requirements.rationale: Generated files, Main branch and CI check names showed only their first ~30 characters.
requirements.statement: A command or a list of paths or names is edited in a field that shows the whole value, wrapping onto further lines as needed; a single-line field whose value is longer than it can show displays the full value on hover.

requirements.rationale: A check with path filters overlapped the next row and 'Add check', and its edit buttons left the screen.
requirements.statement: Each item in a settings list (checks, granted folders and hosts, provider sessions, worktrees, CI check names, spec steps) grows in height to fit its content; no item overlaps another item or the list's add control, and each item's actions stay visible inside its row at 960px.
Errors, warnings and hints shown under or beside a control wrap within the row and never widen it.

requirements.rationale: At 1024px the bar showed 'Vaul' and no way to Jobs or Activity, so settings at the supported width could not be left for those tabs.
requirements.statement: When the project's tabs do not all fit in the top bar, none is cut mid-word, and the ones that do not fit are reachable from an overflow control in the bar.

requirements.rationale: Nothing measured this, which is how it broke unnoticed; the check is what keeps the slice true. It must not depend on files only one checkout has.
requirements.statement: A repeatable check, runnable from a fresh checkout of the repository on this machine with one command, renders every App, Project and Agent settings section with long values at 960px and 1440px, dark and light, and fails naming the section and the element whenever something scrolls sideways, sits outside the window, or leaves a text column under 240px beside its control.

requirements.rationale: The operator approved this list and grouping in the mock (2026-11-10). General held seven groups on one ~5,700px page, so nothing on it was where its name said.
requirements.statement: Project settings lists exactly these sections, under these group headings, in this order: Project — Project, Collaboration, Permissions, Budgets; Agents — Instructions, Charters, Checkpoints, Manager; Landing work — Checks, Landing, Worktrees; Specs and records — Spec steps, Traces, Diagnostics. No section named General, Quality or Runners is listed.

requirements.rationale: A reorganisation that drops a setting is a regression nobody sees until they need it.
requirements.statement: Every setting the General page held appears on exactly one project settings section: name, folder and delete on Project; jobs allowed, hop budget and deliveries per turn on Collaboration; default permissions and granted reach on Permissions; agent budget and token limit on Budgets; the six checkpoint settings on Checkpoints; checks, checks give way and generated files on Checks; main branch, pull-request landing, one commit per build, PR CI as the full check, CI check names, CI interval and CI cutoff on Landing.

requirements.rationale: Links to settings exist in toasts, notices and other screens (General's token limit, a runner error); a removed id must not open a blank page.
requirements.statement: A link or saved location naming a section that no longer exists opens its successor: General, Quality and Runners open Project; an agent's Identity or Charter opens Agent, Execution or Interaction opens Running, Access opens Permissions, Context opens Checkpoints.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-10: a Save stays only where it is needed. Saving Instructions writes and commits AGENTS.md and emptying it asks to confirm, so it is an act rather than a stored value. Confirm buttons inside dialogs (add a check, replace headers, clear traces) are actions, not saves.
requirements.statement: Every setting on project and agent settings applies when it is changed — a text or number field when it is left or Enter is pressed, a long text when it is left — and no section shows a Save button for a setting, except Instructions, which keeps its one Save.
No project or agent settings section renders a native checkbox, a native <select> or a native date input; each such choice uses the app's own switch, toggle, menu or segmented control.

Spec steps shows the steps in order, each built-in step under a title in words (Intake, Requirements, Requirements and acceptance, Acceptance criteria, Approach, Tasks, Build) and marked built in; adding a step, moving or removing one of the operator's steps, changing its sizes, or changing any step's added instruction or a custom step's instructions applies at once, and a change the Hub refuses shows the Hub's reason and leaves the list as the Hub last stored it.

Traces applies the retention, the collector switch and the endpoint on change; replaces the collector headers only through a dialog, never displaying a stored value; and downloads or clears the traces of the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days or all of them, as chosen, with clearing confirmed first.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-10. Permissions and Checkpoints share their names with the project sections they override, which slice 3's inheritance display builds on.
requirements.statement: An agent's settings list exactly five sections — Agent (name, description, last active, charter, archive), Running (model, permission-decision wait, question wait, and Copilot's extras for a Copilot agent), Permissions (default permissions, own granted reach, reading other agents' checkpoints, recall, deciding evidence, keeping the specs true), Checkpoints (checkpoint mode, its own checkpoint point, its checkpoints taken) and Workspace (working directory, its own checkout, provider sessions).

requirements.rationale: With no Runners screen, a menu of existing runners could never reach a model nobody had used yet. Reusing runners keeps the checkpoint and manager menus, which still list runners, from filling with duplicates.
requirements.statement: An agent's Running → Model lists every model of every provider whose coding agent is installed, plus each provider's own default, and choosing one makes the agent's next turn run on that provider and model without a runner having been created first; the Hub reuses an existing runner of the same provider and model rather than adding a second one.
Where an agent has no value of its own for a checkpoint setting or a permission, its section says what the project's value is, and a reset returns it to following the project.
The long-values check from `settings-rows-that-hold-any-value` passes on every new project and agent section at 960 and 1440px, dark and light.

requirements.rationale: The operator often does not know which of the three places holds a setting; a search confined to the open scope would not answer that.
requirements.statement: App, project and agent settings each show a search field above their section list; typing lists every setting across all three scopes that matches by the rule in this document, each result naming the setting, its scope (App, Project or the agent) and its section, label matches listed before description-only matches.

requirements.rationale: With eight agents, one row per agent buries every other result (operator, 2026-11-11).
requirements.statement: A setting every agent has appears once in the results, with the project's non-archived agents listed under it; choosing an agent opens that agent's setting.

requirements.rationale: Ctrl K is where the operator already looks for anything by name.
requirements.statement: The command palette lists matching settings, by the same rule and with the same scope and section, under a Settings group, and choosing one lands on it as a search result does.

requirements.rationale: Finding a setting is not done until the eye is on it; long sections are where it is missed.
requirements.statement: Choosing a result opens the setting's scope and section, scrolls its row into view, highlights the row for at least two seconds, and puts keyboard focus on its control.
A search that matches no setting says that no setting matches the words typed, and lists nothing.
After landing on a setting, the app's location names that setting, so a reload or Back returns to it opened and highlighted as a search would.

requirements.rationale: A reset button alone says something differs, not from what.
requirements.statement: Every setting row whose value is not its default says where its value comes from: on app and project settings 'Changed' with the default it would otherwise have; on an agent setting that follows a project setting, 'Agent's own' with the project's value, or, when the agent has none of its own, 'From project' with that value.

A changed setting returns to the value it would otherwise have (the default, or for an agent the project's) in one action from its row, and the row then shows that value and no longer reads as changed.

requirements.rationale: An agent's own value replaces the project's (reach grants included, hub/hub/reach.py:99), so a project change can silently not apply to it.
requirements.statement: On project settings, default permissions, granted reach, checkpoint mode and checkpoint point each name the non-archived agents that hold their own value for it, each name opening that agent's setting; when none does, nothing is shown.

Each settings scope offers a 'Changed only' view that shows only settings whose value is not its default (for an agent, only its own values), hides sections with none, and says nothing is changed when there is none; turning it off restores the full list.

requirements.rationale: A search kept beside the screens drifts the first time a row is added without it.
requirements.statement: A repeatable check, runnable on this machine with one command, fails naming the scope, section and label of any settings row that a search for its own label does not return, or that a result lands on the wrong row.

The long-values check from `settings-rows-that-hold-any-value` passes on every settings section with the search field, the source marks, the agent names and 'Changed only' shown, at 960 and 1440px, dark and light.

in_scope: Presentation of Environment configuration sections (project and per-agent settings share it)
Typed numeric fields and save feedback
`PUT /projects/{id}/settings` partial-update semantics, runner references, and its history record
non_goals: What each individual setting means: owned by its capability (budgets, checkpointing, checks, conversation titles)
The settings resource as a whole, the main-branch setting's rules and detection, project identity, relocation and deletion: local-project-workspace
Re-attempting integrations when a main branch is named: approval-integration

summary: The project's configuration surface under Environment and the settings write behind it: how each section introduces itself, how settings are laid out as labelled rows, how saving reports its outcome, the main-branch control, that a change may name only the fields it changes, that a runner named in settings must belong to the project, and that a saved change is recorded in the project's history.
title: Project environment settings
